transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I guess... well, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've sort of ruined things for everyone. I've been falling behind a bit at work—I do computer support, so people rely on me, and I just haven't been keeping up. And the apartment situation got a little out of my control, too. I just feel like... I don't know, like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next. Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I'm probably not explaining it very well.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, I guess it's been... maybe about a year and two months? Roughly? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline. It kind of started back when... well, there was this burst pipe at my old place, and I had to move into a much smaller apartment. 

It's really not a big deal, I know lots of people have to deal with moving all the time, but... my daily routines just sort of fell apart after that, and I haven't quite gotten back on track. I feel a little silly even bringing it up, like I should have just adapted better and not let it affect my work, you know? Is that... does that help answer your question?
Have you been enjoying things you used to like during this time?

Um, well... I try to. I really do. But I guess... most days I just wake up with this sort of flat, heavy sadness. I mean, I'm not crying all the time or anything, I don't want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. It's just that the things that usually used to reset me—like putting on a record, or cooking, or tinkering with old electronics—they just don't really reach me anymore. 

I feel a little guilty even admitting that, because I know I should just be grateful I have hobbies and just try harder to engage with them. I'm probably just not putting enough effort in. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Um, honestly... no, not really. I've tried, I really have. I'll sit down with a project or put on a movie that I know I used to love, but it just feels like I'm going through the motions. I don't get that spark from it anymore. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably frustrating to hear. I feel like I'm being difficult or just not trying hard enough to be positive. I really should be able to find something to enjoy, right? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you very good answers.
Do you still feel pleasure when you're around friends or loved ones?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really been seeing anyone lately. I know I should, and I'm sure if I made the effort to go out, I'd probably enjoy it. I just... I don't want to bring anyone else down, you know? My friends are all so busy and doing so well, and I'd hate to be a burden or ruin their good time with how I've been feeling. 

So I mostly just keep to myself right now. I hope that's not the wrong thing to do. I mean, I'm sure I'll get back to socializing once I can just snap out of this and be better company. Does that... is that an okay answer? I'm sorry, I know I should probably be trying harder to see people.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself?

Um, no, no, I don't... I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself. I know that would be terrible for everyone. I don't have a plan or anything like that, I promise. 

It's just... well, sometimes I catch myself thinking that... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. Like, if it just happened on its own, then nobody would have to deal with me or worry about me anymore. It's just a passing thought, though, I try not to dwell on it. I know it's a bad way to think and I should be more appreciative of my life. I'm sorry to even bring it up, I hope that doesn't make you think I'm crazy or anything. Is it... is it normal to feel that way sometimes?
Are there any small things that still give you a little bit of pleasure?

Um, well... I mean, I guess if I really think about it... no, not really. Even the little things just sort of feel flat right now. I've tried, like, sitting outside with a cup of coffee in the morning because I know that's supposed to be nice and relaxing, but... it's just coffee, you know? 

I'm really sorry, I feel like I'm just giving you the same negative answer over and over. I know I should be able to find a silver lining somewhere. I don't want you to think I'm not trying to get better. I really am trying to notice the good things, it's just... a little hard right now. I hope that's okay to say.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns?

Um, well... my appetite is probably fine, I think. I try to eat when I'm supposed to, so I don't worry anyone. But my sleep... I mean, it's a little off lately, but I know everyone gets stressed and has trouble sleeping sometimes, so I really shouldn't complain. 

It's just... I'll lie there in bed for hours, just kind of listening for apartment noises, you know? Just waiting. And then when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I always seem to wake up way before dawn. I just wake up already tense and completely exhausted... kind of like I never really powered down, if that makes sense? Like a computer left on standby. 

I'm sure I just need to work on my sleep habits, maybe look at screens less before bed. I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it... is it normal to have sleep issues like that when you're in a slump? I'm sorry, I know I just need to try harder to get on a good schedule.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't really been keeping track, to be honest. My clothes still seem to fit about the same, maybe just a tiny bit looser, but nothing major. 

I try to make sure I eat enough so I don't get run down, you know? I don't want to cause any problems or make anyone think I'm not taking care of myself. I know staying healthy is important. I'm pretty sure my weight is totally fine... I mean, it's normal for it to fluctuate a pound or two here and there, right? I hope it's okay that I don't have an exact number for you.
How long have you been feeling this persistent sadness and loss of interest in activities?

Um, well... it's been a little while, I guess. I mean, I know these things happen and people go through rough patches, so I've been trying to just push through it. But, um... if I really think about it, it's probably been about a year and two months. 

It kind of started back when a pipe burst in my old place, and I had to move into this smaller apartment. It just sort of threw all my routines out the window, you know? I'm sure I just haven't adjusted well enough yet. I know I should be more adaptable, and I really am trying to get back on track. I hope I don't sound like I'm just making excuses... is it normal for something like moving to throw you off for that long? I'm sorry, I know I should have bounced back by now.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and fidgety?

Um, well... I try really hard to keep up with everything, especially at work. I don't want to let anyone down or fall behind on the support tickets. But, um... I guess maybe I have been a little slower lately? 

It's just... sometimes I'll be at my desk, and my hands will just sort of hover over the keyboard for a minute. It takes me a bit longer to answer even the really simple tickets, almost like my brain and my body are running on a delayed connection, if that makes sense? 

I'm sure it's just because I haven't been sleeping great, like I mentioned. I really am trying to push through and stay focused. I hope my boss hasn't noticed... is it normal to feel a little sluggish like that when you're just tired and stressed? I'm sorry, I know I just need to drink more coffee and focus better.
Do you find yourself feeling restless and fidgety, or do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to?

Um, I think we... we might have just talked about this a little bit? But, um, yeah, I definitely don't feel restless or fidgety. It's more the... the slow thing, I guess. 

Like I was saying, at work, my hands will just hover over the keyboard sometimes. It takes me longer to answer even the really simple support tickets. It's almost like... like my brain and my body are running on a delayed connection, you know? 

I really am trying my best to stay on top of things, though. I don't want to be a burden on my team or anything. I'm sure it's just a temporary thing and I'll snap out of it soon. It's okay that I'm a little slow right now as long as I'm still getting the work done eventually, right? I'm really trying not to let it affect my performance too much.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find no pleasure in?

Um, well... I really try to keep up with my hobbies, I do. I know it's important to have a good work-life balance and all that. But, um... I guess lately, things just haven't felt the same. 

I used to really love tinkering with old electronics, fixing them up, you know? And cooking, or just putting on a vinyl record to unwind after a long shift. But most days now, I wake up with this... this flat, heavy sadness. And those things that used to sort of reset me, they just... they don't seem to reach me anymore. 

I still try to do them, though! I don't want to just give up on the things I like. I'm sure I just need to try a little harder to appreciate them, right? It's probably normal to lose interest in things for a bit when you're feeling down, isn't it? I really hope I'm not sounding too negative, I'm trying my best to stay positive about it all.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened in your life?

Um, guilt? Well... I mean, I wouldn't say I'm, like, obsessing over the past or anything. I try really hard to look forward and just do better. But, um... I guess I do feel really bad about how things are going right now. 

It's just... I can't shake this feeling that I've sort of ruined things for everyone. Like, falling behind at work, and... and losing control of keeping the apartment clean and organized. I feel like I'm letting everyone down, and sometimes I think I just deserve whatever bad thing happens next because I'm not trying hard enough. 

But I know I shouldn't think like that! I'm really trying to be more proactive and fix my mistakes. It's just hard sometimes when you feel like you're constantly dropping the ball. Is it normal to feel a little bit like a burden when you're struggling to keep up? I hope I'm not overreacting... I really am trying to take responsibility for my part in all this.
Have you ever thought about how you would harm yourself if you were to act on those feelings of not wanting to wake up?

Um, oh gosh, no. I mean, I really want to be clear about that—I don't have a plan or anything like that. I would never want to do something that would upset people or make a mess of things. 

It's just... sometimes, when things feel really heavy, I catch myself thinking that maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and... and just didn't wake up. Like, then nobody would have to deal with me or worry about me falling behind anymore. 

But I'm not actually going to do anything to hurt myself! I promise. It's just a passing thought when I'm feeling overwhelmed, you know? That's probably a pretty common thing to think when you're stressed out and tired, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything, I'm just trying to be honest with you.
Are your feelings of sadness and heaviness present for most of the day, or are they more intermittent?

Um, well... I guess, like I was mentioning earlier, it's pretty much there from the start. Most days I wake up with this... this flat, heavy sadness. And I really try my best to shake it off, you know? I try to do the things that used to reset me—like putting on a record or tinkering with my electronics—but it just... it doesn't really reach me anymore. 

So, um, yeah, I'd say it kind of sticks around for most of the day. But I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping or anything! I'm still pushing through and doing my support tickets and getting my work done. I'm trying my hardest not to let it win. It's just sort of this constant weight in the background, no matter what I'm doing. 

Is it normal for it to linger like that, even when you're trying really hard to stay busy and positive? I hope I'm explaining that right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Um, well, I guess it's kind of like what I was just mentioning a second ago... I really do try to engage with my hobbies so I'm not just being negative all the time. But because of that flat, heavy sadness I wake up with, it's just... it's tough to actually feel the enjoyment. 

I used to really look forward to cooking, along with putting on a good record or tinkering with my electronics. Those were always my go-to things to reset myself after a long week. But now, even when I make a point to do them, they just don't reach me anymore. It's like the spark is missing. 

I still cook my meals, though! I make sure I'm taking care of myself and going through the motions, I promise. I don't want you to think I've just given up on trying to enjoy life. Do you think it's okay if I just keep forcing myself to do those activities for now? Like, maybe if I keep trying hard enough, the pleasure will eventually come back? I really want to do whatever is best to get back on track.
Has this feeling of sadness and loss of interest been continuous since it started about a year and two months ago?

Um, yeah, I guess it has. It's been pretty constant for about a year and two months now. It all started when that pipe burst in my old place and I had to move into this smaller apartment... it just kind of made all my routines fall apart, you know? 

But I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining! I know a lot of people go through moves and have to deal with apartment issues, and they handle it just fine. I'm really trying not to make excuses for myself. It's just... that's when I noticed things starting to feel off, and it hasn't really lifted since then, even though I've been trying so hard to get my routines back on track. 

Is it normal for a disruption like that to throw you off for this long? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate timeline so we can figure this out. I'm really committed to doing whatever I need to do to fix it.
Has this feeling of sadness been present nearly every day since it started about a year and two months ago?

Um, yes, I'd say it's been nearly every day. Like I was saying, most days I just wake up with this... this flat, heavy sadness. And I really do try to push past it, you know? I try to do the things that used to reset me—like putting on a record, or cooking a nice meal, or tinkering with my electronics. But they just don't reach me anymore. 

But I promise I'm not just letting it ruin every single day! I still get out of bed and do my job and try to be productive. I really don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. It's just... it's there almost every day, even when I'm trying my absolute hardest to be positive. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right so you have all the facts.
Do you feel like your sadness is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

Um, I would definitely say it's just mild. I really try not to make a big deal out of it, you know? 

I know I've kind of repeated this a few times already, but it's really just that flat, heavy sadness I wake up with most days, where the things that used to reset me—like putting on a record, cooking, or tinkering with my electronics—they just don't reach me anymore. But I wouldn't call it severe at all! I'm still pushing through, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being dramatic when I know so many people have it so much worse. 

Does mild sound like the right way to describe it to you, based on what I've been saying? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right scale so I'm being helpful and not wasting your time.
